headline_marked: Born in 1981, [[Jamaat MP faces criticism]] over 'martyred father' claim
headline: Born in 1981, Jamaat MP faces criticism over 'martyred father' claim
summary: Md Abdul Muntakim claimed his father was martyred in the 1971 Liberation War, but election affidavits show he was born 10 years after the conflict.
details: Jamaat-e-Islami MP Md Abdul Muntakim claimed during a parliamentary budget discussion that his father and grandfather were martyred in the 1971 Liberation War.
However, election affidavits confirm that the Nilphamari-4 MP was born on January 10, 1981, meaning he was born a decade after the war ended.
The MP's comments sparked humorous reactions on social media and criticism from historians and activists.
When questioned about the controversy, Muntakim clarified that his father is actually still alive and that he meant there were martyrs among his grandparents.
He stated, "I didn't literally mean that my father was a martyr," explaining that the martyr he referred to was his father's uncle.
Mofidul Hoque, a trustee of the Liberation War Museum, condemned the statement, calling the presentation of distorted information in parliament unacceptable.
caption:
Born in 1981, a Jamaat MP claimed his father was a 1971 martyr—then clarified his father is still alive.

Jamaat-e-Islami MP Md Abdul Muntakim claimed during a parliamentary budget discussion that his father and grandfather were martyred in the 1971 Liberation War.

However, election affidavits confirm that the Nilphamari-4 MP was born on January 10, 1981, meaning he was born a decade after the war ended.

The MP's comments sparked humorous reactions on social media and criticism from historians and activists.

When questioned about the controversy, Muntakim clarified that his father is actually still alive and that he meant there were martyrs among his grandparents.

He stated, "I didn't literally mean that my father was a martyr," explaining that the martyr he referred to was his father's uncle.

Mofidul Hoque, a trustee of the Liberation War Museum, condemned the statement, calling the presentation of distorted information in parliament unacceptable.

headline_marked: Student's [[body found hanging in school hostel]], sparks vandalism
headline: Student's body found hanging in school hostel, sparks vandalism
summary: A 14-year-old student of Farid Ahmed Bhuiyan Academy in Lakshmipur's Ramganj was found dead; family alleges murder while police suspect suicide.
details: The body of Mehedi Hasan, a 14-year-old class 8 student, was found hanging from a window grill in the hostel of Farid Ahmed Bhuiyan Academy in Ramganj, Lakshmipur.
Police recovered the body on Tuesday afternoon. While authorities suspect the student committed suicide, the family of the deceased has rejected this claim.
Mehedi's father, Zia Uddin, stated that his son was mentally healthy and had no reason to take his own life, alleging that the boy was murdered and the scene was staged as a suicide.
Following reports that the student had been murdered, angry locals vandalized the school's main gate and reception area around 8 PM on Tuesday.
The situation remained tense until midnight, with protesters gathering in front of the school until the administration and police intervened to restore order.
Ramganj Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Kazi Atikur Rahman visited the site and assured the protesters that an investigation is underway to determine the actual cause of death.
Police have deployed additional forces to the area to maintain stability. Necessary action will be taken based on the results of the autopsy report and the ongoing investigation.
caption:
A 14-year-old student found dead in his school hostel sparks outrage and vandalism in Lakshmipur.

The body of Mehedi Hasan, a 14-year-old class 8 student, was found hanging from a window grill in the hostel of Farid Ahmed Bhuiyan Academy in Ramganj, Lakshmipur.

Police recovered the body on Tuesday afternoon. While authorities suspect the student committed suicide, the family of the deceased has rejected this claim.

Mehedi's father, Zia Uddin, stated that his son was mentally healthy and had no reason to take his own life, alleging that the boy was murdered and the scene was staged as a suicide.

Following reports that the student had been murdered, angry locals vandalized the school's main gate and reception area around 8 PM on Tuesday.

The situation remained tense until midnight, with protesters gathering in front of the school until the administration and police intervened to restore order.

Ramganj Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Kazi Atikur Rahman visited the site and assured the protesters that an investigation is underway to determine the actual cause of death.

Police have deployed additional forces to the area to maintain stability. Necessary action will be taken based on the results of the autopsy report and the ongoing investigation.
